title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1973-09-21
lineage: SBD -> Rm -> Reel -> PCM -> DatTransfer Info: Dat (Sony R500) -> Samplitude v6.0 -> Cool Edit Pro v1.2 -> CD -> EAC -> SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a high‑energy 9/21/73 show, highlighted by Let It Grow, He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One and an epic Wharf Rat.
ai_review.review: This 1973 soundboard recording is praised for its crisp, clean mix despite occasional hiss and a few brief cuts. The performance shines with loose, playful improvisations—especially the horn‑enhanced Let It Grow, the blazing He's Gone → Truckin' sequence, and an unforgettable Wharf Rat that many reviewers call “incredible.” Overall the show is regarded as one of the strongest late‑summer ’73 dates.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of 20 reviews are 4–5 stars, consistently praising both the music and the board recording; only minor complaints about hiss or vocal slips keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp and clear overall, with a little extra hiss and a few painful cuts (notably at the end of Playin'). Bass and piano sit low in the mix for some listeners; vocals are occasionally off‑pitch but the horns and drums sit well.

standout_songs: He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One > Wharf Rat
poor_songs: Let Me Sing Your Blues Away (vocals a bit off, considered a weaker bar‑tune)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set builds nicely and ends with a trippy Playin', while the second half explodes—horns join mid‑set for a soaring Let It Grow and the classic sequence that carries the energy to a climactic Wharf Rat and Row Jimmy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for beautiful tone, feeling “no pain,” and a sweet solo on Row Jimmy.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for solid bass work (though mixed low) and strong backing vocals behind Garcia.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith is highlighted as especially “up” for this show; keyboards blend well with the horns.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann receives glowing remarks for clean snare/kick interaction, great timing, and standing out in the mix without being drowned by Mickey.
